title: Winter storm and ice
summary: Ice takes down power lines. Stay warm safely, avoid CO, stay off roads, and watch for hypothermia and frostbite.

sources.title: WTVR: Dominion Energy preps for multi-day outages in winter ice storm (Jan 22, 2026)

blocks.text: In central Virginia the worst winter danger is usually **ice**. Dominion Energy says about **0.25 inch** of ice can be enough to knock out power. Before a January 2026 storm, Dominion warned of multi-day outages statewide.

rows: Heavy snow or ice is possible in the next day or two (issued roughly 12 to 48 hours ahead)
Severe winter conditions have begun or will begin soon (roughly 12 to 24 hours ahead)

items: Stock for several days without power: medicine, pet needs, batteries for radio and flashlights.
Install and test smoke and CO alarms with battery backup.
Weatherproof the home. Learn where your water valves are, in case a pipe bursts.
Keep extra heat sources ready. **Never** use a generator, grill or camp stove inside your home, garage, basement or partly enclosed area.
Check your car: battery, antifreeze, tires, wipers. Keep the gas tank full.
Car kit: blankets, water, snacks, warm clothes, flashlight, first-aid kit, jumper cables, ice scraper, shovel, sand or cat litter for traction, cash, phone power bank, extra medicine.
Stay off the roads. Check 511Virginia.org or call 511 before you travel. If you're trapped in your car, stay in it.
Dress in layers. Mittens are warmer than gloves. Watch for frostbite and hypothermia.
Don't heat with a gas oven or stove. Generators outdoors, 20 feet from the house.
Snow shoveling can trigger a heart attack. Avoid overexertion.
Keep snow clear of vents for fuel-burning appliances.

blocks.text: **Body temperature below 95°F is an emergency.** Signs: shivering, exhaustion, confusion, slurred speech, drowsiness. Call 911. Move the person to a warm room, warm the chest, neck, head and groin first, keep them dry and wrapped in blankets.
**Frostbite:** numb, white, grayish-yellow, firm or waxy skin. Move to a warm room. Warm the area with body heat or warm (not hot) water. **Don't rub or massage it. Don't use a heating pad.**

items: Report downed lines to Dominion at 866-366-4357 and stay 30 feet away.
Let the generator cool before refueling, since fuel spilled on hot parts can ignite.
